# Intro

Real time face detection has a long history, which nowadays has Deep Learning as the main method. The most famous contribution comes from the [Viola-Jones "Robust Real-Time Face Detection"](https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~hic/CS7616/Papers/Viola-Jones-2004.pdf). Even if it has more than 20 years, it is still relevant, expecially for the Computer Vision which relies on Machine Learning.
The paper has 3 main contributions:

## 1. Integral Image

It is an image represetation that allows for a very fast feature evalaution.

## 2. AdaBoost learning algorithm

This classifier can be viewed as a *feature selection process*, achieved using the AdaBoost learning algorithm by constraining each weak classifier to depend on only a single feature.

## 3. Cascade

It is a method for combining successively more complex clasifiers in a cascade structure. Complex processing is reserved only for the promising regions in which a face might occur. The key measure is the *false negative rate* of the attentional process. The structure of the cascaded detection process is the same of a degenerate decision tree.

## Notes

The project is limited to a Machine Learning approach. I would like to use the [YuNet](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11633-023-1423-y.pdf) Deep Learning model, which is lightweight Deep Learning framework developed to run on edge devices. Also, [Raspberry Pi](https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/accessories/ai-camera.html) has a camera sensor which allows users to deploy their own neural network models.

# Dev

Even if the pa

An useful example is the `skimage` documentation, specifically the example [Face classification using Haar-like feature descriptor](https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/auto_examples/applications/plot_haar_extraction_selection_classification.html).

```{python}
from time import time

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import skimage as ski

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

from skimage import data, color
```

`skimage` has the implementation of the integral image algorithm and the HAAR like features cited in the original paper.

```{python}
def extract_feature_image(img, feature_type, feature_coord=None):
    """Extract the haar feature for the current image"""
    ii = ski.transform.integral_image(img)
    return ski.feature.haar_like_feature(
        ii,
        0,
        0,
        ii.shape[0],
        ii.shape[1],
        feature_type=feature_type,
        feature_coord=feature_coord,
    )
```

```{python}
images = ski.data.lfw_subset()
# To speed up the example, extract the two types of features only
feature_types = ['type-2-x', 'type-2-y']

# Compute the result
t_start = time()
X = [extract_feature_image(img, feature_types) for img in images]
X = np.stack(X)
time_full_feature_comp = time() - t_start

# Label images (100 faces and 100 non-faces)
y = np.array([1] * 100 + [0] * 100)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, train_size=150, random_state=0, stratify=y
)

# Extract all possible features
feature_coord, feature_type = ski.feature.haar_like_feature_coord(
    width=images.shape[2], height=images.shape[1], feature_type=feature_types
)
```
